# Purpose

Summarises synthetic daily weather for two cities, reshaping the data with tidyr to compare temperature ranges and count rainy days.

# Inputs

## Data

Reads from **`data/weather_synthetic.csv`** (synthetic).

| Column | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `date` | Observation date |
| `city` | Toronto or Calgary |
| `temp_max_c` | Daily high in Celsius |
| `temp_min_c` | Daily low in Celsius |
| `rain_mm` | Rainfall in millimetres |

## Packages

```{r packages}
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Processing Steps

## 1. Import

```{r import}
weather <- read_csv("data/weather_synthetic.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
```

## 2. Reshape

```{r reshape}
weather_long <- weather %>%
  pivot_longer(c(temp_max_c, temp_min_c),
               names_to = "measure", values_to = "temp_c")
```

## 3. Summarise

```{r summarise}
city_temps <- weather_long %>%
  group_by(city, measure) %>%
  summarise(avg_temp = mean(temp_c), .groups = "drop")

rainy_days <- weather %>%
  group_by(city) %>%
  summarise(rainy_days = sum(rain_mm > 0), .groups = "drop")
```

## 4. Visualise

```{r visualise}
ggplot(weather_long, aes(date, temp_c, colour = measure)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~ city) +
  labs(title = "Daily High and Low", x = NULL, y = "Temperature (C)")
```

# Outputs

- `weather_long` - long-format temperature table
- `city_temps` - average high and low per city
- `rainy_days` - count of days with rain per city
- Faceted line chart

```{r preview-output}
knitr::kable(weather_long)
```
